page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.cm4.2xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated physical cores on an Intel Xeon E5-2667 v4 processor running at 3.2 GHz with an x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates moderate overall performance. The instance achieves average results in single-core Geekbench (1150.0) and Passmark CPU (8118.07) tests, as well as average memory read bandwidth of 414.69 GB/sec for small blocks. However, multi-core performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by stress-ng multi-core (5749.22) and Geekbench multi-core (4273.0) scores falling in the bottom 25%. Memory write bandwidth for large blocks is also weak at 23.56 GB/sec.

The instance is suitable for workloads that benefit from dedicated CPU cores but do not require intensive multi-threaded compute or local storage. Average performance in static web serving (7.11 GB/sec) and Redis SET operations (6.65 million operations/sec) makes it a candidate for basic web serving and caching. However, it is poorly suited for medium-sized LLM inference, where it achieves only 5.29 tokens/sec for text generation, and it exhibits weak performance in database operations.

Operating on the KVM hypervisor, this instance provides a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Benchmark results position the instance in the average tier for single-core tasks, such as Geekbench single-core (1150.0) and static web serving (7.11 GB/sec). However, it exhibits weak multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores falling in the bottom 25%. Memory write bandwidth is also limited to 23.56 GB/sec. Given these characteristics, the ecs.cm4.2xlarge is best suited for moderate general-purpose workloads, basic web serving, and caching operations, while being less optimal for database operations or multi-threaded high-performance computing.
